newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt bourse closes at record high.
newsitem.headline: Egypt bourse closes at record high.

text.p: Egypt's bourse closed at a record high on Tuesday as popular milling shares continued to shine.
The Capital Market Authority's (CMA) overall index closed at 267.11 against 262.60 points on Monday.
On Sunday, the index first broke the previous record of 255.05 set on October 19, 1994.

Turnover was pumped up to 446 million pounds ($131 million), by the transfer of 7.75 million shares in Suez Cement worth 387.5 million in a global depository receipt (GDR) transaction. The shares closed at 56.15 up 1.15.
Brokers had said in September that National Bank of Egypt would sell all or most of its shares in Suez Cement through GDRs in a sale led by ING Barings.

"The market is still booming and moving up. It's a healthy move. Most of the prices are underpriced and just gaining the momentum they should have gained before," said broker Neveen al-Tahery of Delta EAB.

Cairo Pharmaceuticals and Chemicals Industries accounted for 16.28 million pounds of turnover, the second highest after Suez. The company's shares were recently privatised and closed on Monday unchanged at 46.00.
The state had offered investors 708,000 shares of the firm's 3.54 million shares at a minimum of 40 pounds a share for three days from November 19.
"The privatisation steps taking place by the government are pushing the market up like this," said broker Sherif Cararah of EFG-Hermes.
Upper Egypt Flour Mills was the day's third most actively traded stock, rising 1.00 to close at 72.10 in turnover of more than 2.75 million pounds.
Central and West and Delta Flour Mills turnover was 2.60 million pounds and its share closed up 4.00 at 81.00.
East Delta Flour Mills climbed 2.65 pounds to close at 56.00 after trading in shares worth more than 2.34 million pounds.
The CMA index for openly traded firms rose to 404.86 from 392.78 points on Monday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms also rose to 187 from 185.26.
